guide.summary: A budding yeast that stays in one place and drinks dissolved broth.
guide.biology: Many real yeasts live on dissolved food and grow by budding, where a small daughter cell swells out from the side of its parent.
guide.rules: Lives in water or gel and does not swim. Eats broth only, using oxygen; it cannot eat solid protein. Broth comes from the Soluble broth material or from protein broken down by protein enzyme, such as the enzyme Brothmakers release. Comfortable at pH 4.5 to 7, warmth 0.30 to 0.65 and salinity up to 0.25. Fungal inhibitor affects it. Buds off a daughter once it has doubled its body, is at least 30 seconds old and has spare energy. Prey for Amoeba, Rotifer and Wheelgrazer.
guide.example: Put Creambuds on a protein patch with and without Brothmakers nearby and compare how well they grow.
